rationale: B wins because it found a real fourth lane rather than another envelope for the same launch: "Figma's AI now draws the layout from a prompt" uses the assistant fact instead of letting it ride shotgun on the React-export story. A is good, but "Figma's first big swing since the Adobe deal died" smuggles in a "first" the update never gave it and then tells the founder to chase that angle first. B still needs its knuckles rapped for "lands on 4 million desks," but it names more of the proof traps before a reporter does.
gaps_in_A: "Figma's first big swing since the Adobe deal died" and "first major move" invent primacy; the update only says the launch follows the Adobe collapse.

It misses a separate AI-assistant/design-labor angle: the fact that the AI assistant generates layouts from a text prompt is treated as support for the React handoff, not as its own design-work story.
"The Adobe-aftermath angle decays first, so decide on that one today" is too confident without the Adobe-collapse date or any signal that reporters still see it as warm.
"A new product line with its own paid seat reads as evidence of the standalone path" needs an executive willing to talk strategy; otherwise it is a product launch wearing an M&A jacket.
gaps_in_B: "every design and engineering org already paying Figma" assumes paid org relationships; the update says users and Fortune 500 presence, not who pays.
"it lands on 4 million desks" inflates a company-stated user count into distribution for the assistant/Make, even though the $25 Make seat implies adoption is unknown.
"faster work, fewer hours billed for it" is a plausible tension, but it is not in the facts. Keep the labor question; don't sell the outcome.
